chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Charlie Christian in Oklahoma City
summary: McGhee describes Christian's natural feeling and tune 'Solo Flight', and meeting him in 1933-34.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you what. Charlie Christian helped a lot. He helped Oklahoma quite a bit as far as the sound is concerned. Because he had a thing going which was natural for him, but I mean, like that was really a natural for everybody that listened to what he was playing. Like, when he came out of Oklahoma, he upset... He upset the nation, in fact, in a way, because he was playing terrifically. I mean, everything that he played had that
feeling [SINGS CHARLIE CHRISTIAN 4 BARS]. Well, everybody could have played in that rhythm and (?) all the time, but they never put it in music like he did.
Which tune are you talking about?
I'm just talking about the figure.
Yeah, the ending of "Solo Flight". [SINGS IT] Hell, we used to do that all the time! But he did it right.
But some people have said that he listened to Prez, too.
Oh, I wouldn't doubt that. I mean, because he and Prez always... Through whatever he was doing, you'd hear Prez's sound. Well, his brother played piano.

Yeah. Ed Christian. He played piano, so he had a thing going with him, too. But Charlie was... He had a natural thing going. Cats used to come around and look for Charlie when they'd come to Oklahoma City. They wanted to show him like... Some cat Louis who played guitar with (what was that girl there?) Julia Lee, I think her name was, from Kansas City... He played in her band, and they would come to Oklahoma City to play dances. And whenever they'd come there, Charlie would look up the guitar player, because

he had to talk about...you know what I mean, he'd show him what's happening. And everybody would come find him, too. If he didn't go look for them, they'd come find him, because everybody told them, "When you get to Oklahoma City, make sure you go to meet Charlie Christian." He could play his can off, man.
When did you first hear him and meet him?

In Oklahoma City. Yeah, this was back in maybe 1933 or 1934. Like I said, my uncle had a grocery store there that my father had...he had helped him get into business. And the reason why he was called my uncle... He was not my uncle, but he was called my uncle because he married my father's sister.
So he was like a step-uncle.
Yeah, like a far removed...something like that! But anyway, that's the way it was.
